explanation: Sort the values, fix one position, and move two pointers through the remaining suffix. Skip repeated fixed values and pointer values after each match so every triple appears once.
timeComplexity: O(n squared) time for n values. Sorting costs O(n log(n+1)); for each fixed index the two pointers cross its suffix once, for O(n squared) total work.
spaceComplexity: O(log n) sort stack excluding output; at most O(n squared) output. Besides the result triples, storage comes from the language sorting routine.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 C++ algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: For a fixed sorted first value, moving the left pointer raises the candidate sum and moving the right pointer lowers it. Thus every discarded pair cannot complete a zero sum. Skipping equal fixed values and equal pair endpoints after a match avoids duplicates while retaining one representative of every distinct valid triple.
walkthrough: For [-3,-1,0,1,2,4], fixing -3 finds pairs (-1,4) and (1,2). Fixing -1 later finds (0,1). Return the three triples [-3,-1,4],[-3,1,2],[-1,0,1], with any allowed triple order.
edgeCases: Three distinct positions are required, even if some values are equal.
Duplicate values must not create duplicate triples.
Fewer than three values produce no triple.
